clue.text: Standing up fairly well

definitions.meaning: recovered after an illness, back to reasonable health

explanation.surface: Someone upright and in reasonable health.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom covers both being upright on two legs and being recovered enough to get about again after illness.

clue.text: Course -brother returned to take it

indicators.note: returned means the word for brother is sent back the way it came, read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A brother comes back along a route to collect something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns BRO into ORB; 'to take' simply joins it to IT.
explanation.definitionFit: A planet's course round the sun is its path of revolution.

clue.text: Port-grab one on the quiet for a flier

parts.note: Oran is a port in Algeria
to grab is to get
the Roman numeral I is one
P stands for piano, musical shorthand for quietly

explanation.surface: Someone in a harbour quietly snatches something for an airman.
explanation.walkthrough: ORANGE-TIP is a British butterfly, hence 'flier'; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This butterfly, named for the orange patches on the male's wingtips, is a creature that flies.

clue.text: Liquor brewed in Red Line Brewery

indicators.note: brewed suggests the letters of the brewery name are stewed and mixed into something new

explanation.surface: A drink made at a brewery called Red Line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brewed in' tells you to rearrange REDLINEBREWERY.
explanation.definitionFit: A homemade fermented drink from small dark fruit is a type of alcoholic liquor.

clue.text: Did without holding up Newcastle

indicators.note: holding means one piece wraps round the other and contains it

parts.note: a fort is a castle or stronghold

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word new is written bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone managed without supporting Newcastle, the football club.
explanation.walkthrough: The trick is to split Newcastle into New and castle; 'up', in a down clue, reverses New, and 'holding' puts the result inside the castle word.
explanation.definitionFit: To forgo something is to abstain from it or go without it; the past tense matches.

clue.text: Couch intended for a particular purpose

definitions.meaning: to couch an idea is to put it into words
as in an ... purpose or intention, specific and deliberate

explanation.surface: A sofa made for one particular job.
explanation.definitionFit: To couch is to phrase or articulate something, and an express aim is specific and deliberate.

clue.text: Notes returned with something 1 ac

indicators.note: returned means the word for notes is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: doh is the first note of the sol-fa scale, so dohs are notes

explanation.surface: Musical notes sent back with a cross-reference.
explanation.walkthrough: '1 ac' is 1 across, on one's feet; the definition means with something on one's feet, i.e. wearing shoes.
explanation.definitionFit: Being wearing footwear is having something on the feet.

clue.text: House let in pieces

parts.note: a building whose rooms are rented out one at a time to guests

explanation.definitionFit: An inn or guest house rents out its rooms separately, a night at a time.

clue.text: Working man ceased to work in metal

indicators.note: working suggests the letters are worked over and rearranged

explanation.surface: A labourer stopped working at a metal job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Working' tells you to rearrange MANCEASED; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To damascene is to ornament steel or iron with inlaid gold or silver patterns, a metalworking craft.

clue.text: Decide to use cosmetics continuously without mummy's minding at, heart

annotationWithheld.why: Decide to use cosmetics continuously without mummy's minding at, heart: as held (stray comma, garbled OCR) no parse gives MAKE UP ONE'S MIND; MAKE UP + ON fits but the rest does not build ES MIND
annotationWithheld.clue: Decide to use cosmetics continuously without mummy's minding at, heart

clue.text: March sees the introduction of a guest

indicators.note: sees the introduction of means a piece is brought in and placed within the other word

parts.note: a march is a border or frontier region

explanation.surface: In March a visitor arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'March' looks like the month, but it means a frontier: BORDER, with A put in.
explanation.definitionFit: A lodger who pays for meals and a room is a paying guest in someone's house.

clue.text: A shade you might call buff? Brown?. .

indicators.note: you might call signals that the words are spoken, so we go by how they sound

parts.note: a buff is a fan, and Brown suggests Tom, as in Tom Brown, the schoolboy hero; together they are said as fan-tom

explanation.surface: Naming colours: is this shade buff, or brown?
explanation.walkthrough: Buff and brown look like colour shades, but a shade here is a ghost. Tom Brown's Schooldays is a classic Victorian novel about a boy at Rugby School.
explanation.definitionFit: A shade is a ghost or spirit, an apparition of the dead.

clue.text: … Stone? Grey? See it in a mixture

indicators.note: in a mixture means the letters are mixed together and rearranged

explanation.surface: Musing over a grey stone and how it looks when mixed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a mixture' tells you to rearrange GREY, SEE and IT.
explanation.definitionFit: This golden-brown banded quartz is a semi-precious gem.

clue.text: Without capital, Bell is still a Bell

indicators.note: without capital means the capital letter at the start of these words is left off, and the rest of the run is kept

explanation.surface: Losing its capital letter, a Bell remains a Bell.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the capital B from 'Bell is'. Emily Brontë published under the pseudonym of Bell, with that first name; her sisters were Currer and Acton Bell.
explanation.definitionFit: Emily Brontë's pen name had this as its first name and Bell as its surname.

clue.text: Name the French bestowed on a bird

indicators.note: bestowed on means the French article is placed next to the bird, following it

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A French name given to a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bestowed on' puts the French article after the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A heading or appellation by which a book or person is known.

clue.text: Trite but not necessarily true, according to the Bellman

definitions.text: not necessarily true, according to the Bellman
definitions.meaning: in Lewis Carroll's The Hunting of the Snark the Bellman says what I tell you three times is true, so saying it only two times proves nothing

explanation.surface: Something hackneyed and possibly false, says Carroll's Bellman.
explanation.definitionFit: A story repeated often is hackneyed, and to the Bellman only a threefold telling made it certain.

clue.text: Fury — is it about ring?

indicators.note: about means the words is it are turned round and read backwards

parts.note: to ring someone is to phone them

explanation.surface: Someone angry wonders whether it's about a phone call.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns ISIT into TISI, then add PHONE.
explanation.definitionFit: She was one of the three Erinyes of Greek myth, avenging spirits.

clue.text: Start to make a speech without a single drink

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside means the speech word surrounds the others

parts.note: to orate is to make a speech
I is one, a single
gin is a drink

explanation.surface: Beginning a speech without even one drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not 'lacking'.
explanation.definitionFit: To begin or arise; both verbs mean come into being.

clue.text: Seconds are tense

definitions.meaning: goods sold off cheaply because flawed
the grammatical tense for continuing past action, I was walking

explanation.surface: Seconds are nervous.
explanation.definitionFit: Flawed goods are sold as seconds, and in grammar it names the continuous past tense.

clue.text: Was a blood donor after girl made it possible

indicators.note: after means the donor word follows the girl's name

parts.note: Ena is a girl's name
a blood donor has bled

explanation.surface: A girl's blood donation made something possible.
explanation.walkthrough: Ena is a stock crossword girl's name; 'after' sets the donor word behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: To allow or permit something is to empower it to happen.

clue.text: Piece that often commands complete attention, turning all heads

indicators.note: heads means take the first letter of each of the words that come before it

parts.words: that often commands complete attention, turning all

explanation.surface: A musical piece that often grabs everyone's attention, turning every head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all heads' picks the first letters of 'that often commands complete attention, turning all'.
explanation.definitionFit: A keyboard composition showing off a player's touch is a musical piece.

clue.text: Racket I have to make enquiries about

indicators.note: about means the enquiry word goes round the letter I

parts.note: to nose is to pry, to make enquiries

explanation.surface: Someone with a racket says I must investigate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts NOSE round I; 'have to' is linking.
explanation.definitionFit: A din or loud clamour is a racket.

clue.text: Push bridge player out, holding nothing

parts.note: E is East, one of the four bridge players

indicators.note: holding means the out word contains the nothing

parts.note: LBW, leg before wicket, is a way of being out in cricket
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Shove a bridge player out, holding no cards.
explanation.walkthrough: LBW (leg before wicket) is a way a batsman is out in cricket; 'holding' puts O inside it after E.
explanation.definitionFit: To nudge or jostle with the arm is to shove someone.

clue.text: Harry has no right to the device

indicators.note: has no means a letter is removed from the word

parts.note: to badger is to harry or pester

explanation.surface: Harry lacks the right to use a gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry' looks like a name but is a verb, BADGER; 'has no' takes away R.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry an emblem or insignia is called a device.

clue.text: What is added in case small company's in trouble

indicators.note: trouble suggests the letters are disturbed and jumbled

parts.note: CO is short for company

explanation.surface: Something added to the case in case a small firm runs into trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' tells you to rearrange CASE, S, CO and IN.
explanation.definitionFit: An acquisition added to a library or museum collection is an addition.

clue.text: Wind up without a motive

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the letters are read bottom to top, backwards
without means the letter A is dropped

parts.note: a reason is a motive

explanation.surface: Getting worked up for no reason at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' takes A out of REASON leaving RESON, which 'up' turns backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailors call a strong headwind a dead one of these, blowing straight on the bows.

clue.text: First, for instance, speaking about 20

indicators.note: about means the speaking word wraps round the other

parts.note: oral means spoken
the cross-reference is to 20 across, a racket, and din is a racket

explanation.surface: Someone first talks about the number twenty.
explanation.walkthrough: '20' is a cross-reference to 20 across, whose answer means a racket.
explanation.definitionFit: First is an example of a number showing position in a sequence.

clue.text: Creatures hit in a setback

indicators.note: setback means the whole run of letters is sent back, read in reverse

parts.note: to slam is to hit

explanation.surface: Animals struck during a setback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setback' reverses SLAM IN A as one run.
explanation.definitionFit: Beasts are living creatures.

clue.text: Expected to end in mortal combat

parts.note: due means expected, as a train is due

indicators.note: end in means take the last letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Sure to finish in fatal fighting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end in mortal' gives L.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal fight between two people is single combat.

clue.text: Man who wrote II Kings

parts.note: two kings: the first is Edward, a name of many English monarchs
the second king is Lear, Shakespeare's king

explanation.surface: Who was the author of the biblical book II Kings?
explanation.walkthrough: II Kings looks like the Old Testament book, but means two kings. The poet wrote nonsense verse such as The Owl and the Pussy-cat.
explanation.definitionFit: He was a Victorian nonsense writer and artist, author of limericks.
